headline: Google's quantum team has shown on real hardware a way to make the special quantum building blocks that error-corrected computers need with far less error and far fewer qubits.
score_reason: Peer-reviewed in Science, first hardware demonstration of a long-predicted technique; verified from a detailed trade report.
importance_line: This is a hardware proof of an idea Google proposed in theory in 2024, and it points to future error-corrected quantum computers needing fewer qubits, which matters first to quantum researchers and hardware companies; it is one lab's result on a small code and does not by itself show a full-scale machine.
summary: Quantum Computing Report reports that Google Quantum AI, in a study published in Science, ran a technique called magic state cultivation on its Willow superconducting chip, cutting errors about 40-fold and reaching a record 99.99% fidelity (a measure of how accurate a quantum state is) for the special "T-states" that universal quantum computers require. Until now such states were expected to take up 90% to 95% of a fault-tolerant machine's qubits when made by the older distillation method, while cultivation uses a small error-checking code and then moves the cleaned state into a larger one.
